kid.question: Where does Isaiah call people to praise the Lord?

options.text: Only inside Jerusalem
Across wilderness and islands
Only beside the sea
Only in the temple

kid.explanation: Isaiah invites wilderness settlements, mountains, and islands to praise the Lord.

kid.question: What does the Lord promise to make light for the blind?

options.text: A carved image
A dry river
Darkness
A prison door

kid.explanation: The Lord moves from long silence to action and promises to guide the blind through unknown paths.

kid.question: What is wrong with the people who have eyes and ears?

options.text: They cannot see any light
They have no teachers
They cannot speak to one another
They do not truly notice or listen

kid.explanation: Isaiah challenges people who have eyes and ears yet fail to observe or hear.

kid.question: Why had Israel become prey to robbers in this passage?

options.text: They would not walk in the Lord’s ways
They had too few walls
They had traveled too far
They could not hear a trumpet

kid.explanation: The people’s captivity is connected to refusing the Lord’s ways, yet they fail to take the warning to heart.

kid.question: What does the Lord promise in deep water and fire?

options.text: You will find a safer route
I will be with you
They will become a road
They will hide you from enemies

kid.explanation: The Redeemer calls Israel by name and promises His presence through waters and fire.

kid.question: From where will the Lord gather His people?

options.text: Only from the east
Only from the temple
From every direction
Only from the desert

kid.explanation: The Lord promises to gather His people from every direction because they belong to Him.

kid.question: What are the people called to be for the Lord?

options.text: Carpenters
Prison guards
Rival gods
Witnesses

kid.explanation: Israel is called to witness that the Lord declared and saved, unlike rival gods.

kid.question: What path does the Lord say He made?

options.text: A path through the sea
A tunnel through a mountain
A bridge over Babylon
A road around the desert

kid.explanation: The Lord identifies Himself as Israel’s redeemer and recalls a way through the sea that overcame armed power.

kid.question: What new thing will the Lord provide in the desert?

options.text: A stronger idol
A way and water
A higher throne
A deeper prison

kid.explanation: The Lord announces a new thing: a way in the wilderness and water in the desert.

kid.question: Why does water flow in the wilderness?

options.text: To flood the cities
To power a mill
To give the Lord’s people drink
To hide a treasure

kid.explanation: The new water is given in the wilderness so the Lord’s chosen people can drink.

high-school.question: What is the effect of naming distant places in the call to praise?

options.text: The message excludes people in cities
The wilderness is the only holy place
The Lord’s glory is proclaimed beyond one city
The islands are warned to stay silent

high-school.explanation: Isaiah invites wilderness settlements, mountains, and islands to praise the Lord.

high-school.question: How does the promise to guide the blind qualify the fierce imagery just before it?

options.text: The Lord’s anger is aimed at every blind person
The blind must find the path without help
The guidance comes from the idols
The Lord’s action includes guidance and rescue

high-school.explanation: The Lord moves from long silence to action and promises to guide the blind through unknown paths.

high-school.question: What distinction is Isaiah making with seeing but not observing?

options.text: Receiving signs is different from attending to them
Physical sight is a guarantee of understanding
The people have been given no message
Hearing matters only when sight fails

high-school.explanation: Isaiah challenges people who have eyes and ears yet fail to observe or hear.

high-school.question: What makes the description of burning especially troubling?

options.text: The fire was treated as an ordinary household flame
The people suffered yet still did not take it to heart
The captors offered to restore them
The people asked for help from the wrong ruler

high-school.explanation: The people’s captivity is connected to refusing the Lord’s ways, yet they fail to take the warning to heart.

high-school.question: What is the comfort in “I have called thee by thy name”?

options.text: Only named leaders may cross the waters
The people must earn a new name
The people are personally known and claimed by their Redeemer
The Lord has forgotten their earlier covenant

high-school.explanation: The Redeemer calls Israel by name and promises His presence through waters and fire.

high-school.question: What does the four-direction gathering show about the promise?

options.text: Only people near Jerusalem can return
The Lord chooses one direction as holy
The gathering is limited to soldiers
Distance will not prevent the Lord’s claim on His people

high-school.explanation: The Lord promises to gather His people from every direction because they belong to Him.

high-school.question: What should Israel’s witness establish in the gathering of nations?

options.text: The Lord declared and saved; He alone is God
Israel’s own strength secured its rescue
The nations missed an earlier warning
A human king planned the rescue

high-school.explanation: Israel is called to witness that the Lord declared and saved, unlike rival gods.

high-school.question: Why recall the sea path while promising action against Babylon?

options.text: Babylon had already built the sea path
A past deliverance supports trust in a new one
The people must repeat every detail of the earlier journey
The sea is safer than every desert

high-school.explanation: The Lord identifies Himself as Israel’s redeemer and recalls a way through the sea that overcame armed power.

high-school.question: Why does Isaiah say not to dwell on former things just after recalling the sea?

options.text: The old deliverance was a mistake
The Lord has stopped guiding His people
The people should recognize a fresh act of deliverance
The coming act has no relation to the past

high-school.explanation: The Lord announces a new thing: a way in the wilderness and water in the desert.

high-school.question: How does the response of wild creatures deepen the picture of renewal?

options.text: Only wild creatures receive the water
The people become less important than the animals
The creatures create the rivers themselves
Even the nonhuman world honors the giver of water

high-school.explanation: The new water is given in the wilderness so the Lord’s chosen people can drink.

expert.question: How does the geographical spread of praise continue the “new song” of verse 10?

options.text: The praise retreats from the nations to one sanctuary
The named places mark the limits of the servant’s work
The landscape replaces human witnesses
The response to the Lord’s action expands toward the world’s edges

expert.explanation: Isaiah invites wilderness settlements, mountains, and islands to praise the Lord.

expert.question: What tension does the passage hold between the warrior cry and the guiding hand?

options.text: Divine intervention judges enemies while refusing to abandon the vulnerable
The Lord first guides the nations, then forgets Israel
The warrior image cancels the promise of guidance
Both images describe the same human army

expert.explanation: The Lord moves from long silence to action and promises to guide the blind through unknown paths.

expert.question: Why does the passage call the Lord’s own servant blind?

options.text: The servant’s eyes were removed as a punishment
Covenant status does not prevent failure to perceive and obey
The title “servant” now refers only to foreign idols
Blindness is praised as the ideal way to learn

expert.explanation: Isaiah challenges people who have eyes and ears yet fail to observe or hear.

expert.question: How do the question “Who will give ear?” and the unheeded fire interpret the disaster?

options.text: The disaster proves the Lord had no role in history
The fire is only a weather report
The crisis is also a failure to learn from covenant correction
The people have already responded fully to the warning

expert.explanation: The people’s captivity is connected to refusing the Lord’s ways, yet they fail to take the warning to heart.

expert.question: How do “Fear not” and the water and fire images fit together?

options.text: The images show that danger was only imagined
The command asks Israel to cross without divine aid
The promise concerns water but leaves fire unanswered
Redemption promises presence through danger, not the absence of danger

expert.explanation: The Redeemer calls Israel by name and promises His presence through waters and fire.

expert.question: How do the directional commands serve the statement “Fear not: for I am with thee”?

options.text: They turn personal reassurance into a comprehensive gathering promise
They replace reassurance with a map of conquest
They say the people must gather themselves without God
They confine God’s presence to the east

expert.explanation: The Lord promises to gather His people from every direction because they belong to Him.

expert.question: How does the witness scene answer the blindness language of verse 8?

options.text: Blindness disqualifies Israel from every future role
Those summoned to perceive can testify from the Lord’s saving acts
The court asks Israel to praise foreign gods
The witness is a craftsman defending his image

expert.explanation: Israel is called to witness that the Lord declared and saved, unlike rival gods.

expert.question: How does the recollection of defeated chariots function in the announcement about Babylon?

options.text: It claims Babylon and Egypt were the same army
It shifts responsibility for redemption to Israel’s weapons
It presents the Lord’s earlier mastery over empire as grounds for future hope
It implies the coming action can only occur at sea

expert.explanation: The Lord identifies Himself as Israel’s redeemer and recalls a way through the sea that overcame armed power.

expert.question: What is the relationship between the sea path and the new desert rivers?

options.text: The former rescue is denied so the new one can be believed
Both descriptions concern the same location and moment
The new rivers show that the sea path was unnecessary
The earlier rescue is a pattern, while the promised rescue exceeds mere repetition

expert.explanation: The Lord announces a new thing: a way in the wilderness and water in the desert.

expert.question: Why include animals honoring God beside the people’s need for water?

options.text: The provision is both practical rescue and a sign of divine glory in creation
The animals are the only true witnesses of redemption
The water exists mainly to remove the animals from the desert
The image narrows the promised change to a single spring

expert.explanation: The new water is given in the wilderness so the Lord’s chosen people can drink.
